title: sci-RNA-seq
scope: Cao 2017 sci-RNA-seq implementation: the depicted two-round cellular combinatorial-indexing route, with primary-supported PCR introduction of the second barcode. Cells and recovered nuclei are supported starting preparations. The separate three-level indexed-Tn5 variant in Cao 2017 and later sci-RNA-seq3 are outside this depicted route. Adjacent SPLiT-Seq, CEL-Seq, and the EdU legend are outside the assigned schematic. The single-cell/poly(A)-RNA icon identifies the biological target rather than a separate extraction operation.

states.label: Second-round well preparations containing double-stranded cDNA

evidence.locator: sci-RNA-Seq row: second wells → 2nd strand synthesis arrow

evidence.quote: Second strand synthesis, transposition with Tn5 transposase, lysis, and PCR amplification are performed. The PCR primers target the barcoded polyT primer on one end, and the Tn5 adaptor insertion on the other end, such that resulting PCR amplicons preferentially capture the 3’ ends of transcripts. These primers introduce a second barcode, specific to each well of the PCR plate.

operations.label: Reverse transcribe RNA with first-round barcode and UMI primers
operations.description: In each first-round well, synthesize cDNA from cellular or nuclear RNA using that well’s indexed poly(T) primers; the resulting cDNA is retained with the cellular or nuclear preparation.

operations.information_effect: The DNA copy preserves transcript sequence together with the first well’s index and UMI; cells within that well share the index.

operations.label: Tn5-tag cDNA, lyse, and amplify with second-round indexed PCR primers
operations.description: In the separate second-round wells, perform Tn5 transposition, lysis, and PCR to yield amplified sequencing libraries. The primary paper assigns second-round well indexing to PCR, resolving the diagram’s transposome-centered shorthand.
operations.mechanism: Tn5 transposition precedes lysis and PCR. PCR targets the barcoded RT-primer end and a Tn5 insertion end; the second cellular barcode is contributed by the PCR primers.
operations.information_effect: Sequencing-compatible DNA fragments carry transcript sequence, UMI, and the RT/PCR barcode combination; retention of compartment boundaries is no longer needed once this combination is encoded.

method_scopes.rationale: The row title and single-cell combinatorial indexed RNA sequencing caption identify sci-RNA-seq. Cao 2017 [b00007–b00010] directly describes this two-round route for cells or nuclei. Its explicit third-level variant has another pooling/sorting round absent here; it does not expand the assigned target. The parallel wells are retained as a collection with internal partitions; colors indicate indices, not isolated chemical fractions. The broad adapter block remains composite, with second-strand synthesis separately shown upstream. PCR indexing resolves the transposome depiction as recorded in the Correction.

Pilot-selected primary candidate PMID 28818938 for sci-RNA-seq. This selection is not scientific evidence of method identity or mechanism.
Here we developed a combinatorial indexing method to uniquely label the transcriptomes of large numbers of single cells or nuclei (sci-RNA-seq).

A first molecular index is introduced to the mRNA of cells within each well with in situ reverse transcription (RT) incorporating a barcode-bearing, well-specific polyT primer containing unique molecular identifiers (UMI).

Second strand synthesis, transposition with Tn5 transposase, lysis, and PCR amplification are performed. The PCR primers target the barcoded polyT primer on one end, and the Tn5 adaptor insertion on the other end, such that resulting PCR amplicons preferentially capture the 3’ ends of transcripts. These primers introduce a second barcode, specific to each well of the PCR plate.

Amplicons are pooled and subjected to massively parallel sequencing, resulting in 3’-tag digital gene expression profiles, with each read associated with two barcodes corresponding to the first and second rounds of cellular indexing (Fig. 1B).

corrections.diagram_observation: The diagram places “Well-specific transposomes” within “2nd index tagging and sequencing adapters”, between strands labeled “i5 adapter with cell index” and “i7 adapter with cell index”; its caption attributes another set of well-specific barcodes to this block. PCR is not explicitly named. The row shows two cell-distribution rounds and a final library labeled Index 2, Index 1, UMI, cDNA.
corrections.primary_statement: For the two-level route, Cao 2017 [b00009] reports second-strand synthesis, Tn5 transposition, lysis, and then PCR, and explicitly says the PCR primers introduce the second barcode specific to the PCR well. [b00023] separately describes an indexed-Tn5 third-level variant with an additional pool/sort round. The asserted route therefore uses PCR for second-round indexing, retains Tn5 for adapter insertion, and does not instantiate that unshown extra variant.
